# `prefer-allocator-dupe`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports allocator `print` and `printSentinel` calls, and legacy
`std.fmt.allocPrint` and `allocPrintSentinel` calls, that only duplicate a
string.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Direct duplication allocates the required bytes and copies once, avoiding the
formatter and its growing output buffer.

## When it fires

The replacement uses `allocator.dupe(u8, ...)` or `allocator.dupeSentinel(u8,
..., 0)`.

The format must be a brace-free literal or exactly `"{s}"` with one argument.
Sentinel calls are rewritten only when their final argument is `0`. Allocator
methods require an explicitly typed allocator binding or a receiver with a
recognized allocator role; writer `print` calls stay unchanged. Calls with other
formatting specifiers or escaped format braces stay unchanged.

```zig
// Before
const copy = try allocator.print("{s}", .{name});
const terminated = try allocator.printSentinel("literal", .{}, 0);

// After
const copy = try allocator.dupe(u8, name);
const terminated = try allocator.dupeSentinel(u8, "literal", 0);
```

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn copy(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, name: []const u8) ![]u8 {
    return std.fmt.allocPrint(allocator, "{s}", .{name});
}
```
